paragraphs: Last Sunday Grandpa took us to the war memorial and spoke about the [[violence:violence]] and long [[conflict:conflict]] of his childhood.
One [[night:night]], he said, a sudden [[raid:raid]] revealed the full [[enormity:enormity]] of the pain behind brave words.
He described a winter [[campaign:campaign]] that ended in one final [[battle:battle]] beside the frozen river.
My little brother shivered as he heard of the [[quiet:quiet]] [[struggle:struggle]] and the distant [[explosion:explosion]].
Soldiers would [[bombard:bombard]] the town, while planes flew over to [[bomb:bomb]] the bridges at [[night:night]].
Each [[blast:blast]] made the windows [[burst:burst]] and sent small children crying beneath the tables.
Even now, a tiny [[spark:spark]] from a [[stove:stove]] [[twinkle:twinkles]] in Grandpa's sad memories.
He remembered the smell of [[gunpowder:gunpowder]] rising from a wrecked [[tank:tank]] in an open [[field:field]].
A heavy [[cannon:cannon]] stood silent in the hall, and a small [[missile:missile]] lay beside it.
Grandpa gently placed an old [[weapon:weapon]] and a worn [[pistol:pistol]] into a [[wooden:wooden]] box.
Next to them lay a rusty [[rifle:rifle]] and one [[bullet:bullet]], sad souvenirs of those days.
Finally he pointed to a [[target:target]] that once helped shells [[deflect:deflect]] away from nearby homes.
Grandpa's [[first:first]] [[mission:mission]] was to carry letters, guided by the warm [[flame:flame]] of a lamp.
One evening a red [[flare:flare]] rose, and its [[glitter:glitter]] fell softly across the dark sky.
By the soft [[glow:glow]] of that light he cleaned his [[blade:blade]] slowly after [[supper:supper]].
Then he would lay his [[sword:sword]] and old [[axe:axe]] beside the [[quiet:quiet]] [[fireplace:fireplace]].
With a small [[hammer:hammer]] he once fixed the [[bow:bow]] that played music on cold evenings.
Years later, a bent [[arrow:arrow]] and a long [[spear:spear]] lay under the dusty classroom pictures.
A cracked [[helmet:helmet]] and a dented [[shield:shield]] rest side by side above the school door.
Kind teachers helped [[equip:equip]] the children and [[prepare:prepare]] warm tea for tired visitors.
The hall could [[provide:provide]] hot soup and [[deploy:deploy]] friendly helpers at the gate.
No stone has [[hit:hit]] the wall since then, and no drum has [[beat:beat]] for marching armies.
No sudden [[strike:strike]] has been heard, and no angry fist has [[punch:punched]] holes in doors.
Hands that once used to [[chop:chop]] wood will never [[stab:stab]] a friend in anger.
That hard [[dilemma:dilemma]] left Grandpa's whole family in a lasting [[plight:plight]] for years.
Every hidden [[pitfall:pitfall]] sprang from a [[cruel:cruel]] [[conspiracy:conspiracy]] among greedy leaders.
Streets grew [[destitute:destitute]], and a long [[famine:famine]] spread slowly through the [[valley:valley]].
Thin children would [[starve:starve]] when cold nights [[deprive:deprived]] them of warm meals.
Strong men came to [[seize:seize]] the [[grain:grain]] and [[pursue:pursue]] poor farmers down the lanes.
Each new [[threat:threat]] would [[offend:offend]] the calm folks who loved their [[quiet:quiet]] country life.
Yet no [[aggressive:aggressive]] shouts could ever [[invade:invade]] their small house full of love.
No outsider dared [[trespass:trespass]] past the [[fence:fence]] or [[intrude:intrude]] into their yard.
The family's kind rules were never [[violate:violated]], even when angry crowds [[attack:attacked]] the old peace.
Each sudden [[assault:assault]] only taught them to [[challenge:challenge]] spite with calm, patient words.
A long [[siege:siege]] failed to [[surround:surround]] the town with hunger, and a young [[guard:guard]] kept watch at the gate.
Even the high walls could not [[enclose:enclose]] their hope through the long [[pause:pause]] in the talks.
Long after, the town built an exact [[replica:replica]] of the old gate in the square.
At last the guns would [[halt:halt]], and the sad songs would slowly [[cease:cease]].
Brave mothers would [[oppose:oppose]] the spite, and the crowds no longer tried to [[oppress:oppress]] the weak.
Wise words could [[counter:counter]] the fear and [[deter:deter]] young men from joining the fights.
Old laws would [[forbid:forbid]] guns, and city schools [[prohibit:prohibited]] games with knives.
Calm leaders tried to [[prevent:prevent]] further [[loss:loss]], while farmers began to [[revolt:revolt]] softly.
No son would [[betray:betray]] a friend, and no [[treason:treason]] would [[stain:stain]] the family name.
One young [[rebel:rebel]] refused the [[praise:praise]] offered by a hired [[traitor:traitor]] across the river.
Each true [[patriot:patriot]] carried no [[blame:blame]] for the sad faults of their leaders.
A soft [[reproach:reproach]] spoke louder than the cold [[evidence:evidence]] laid upon the table.
Clear [[proof:proof]] ended the idle [[terror:terror]] once felt by children who loved nightly stories.
The news was [[terrible:terrible]], yet the will for peace grew [[terrific:terrific]] in every heart.
One [[horrible:horrible]] noise woke sharp [[alarm:alarm]] inside each tiny [[wooden:wooden]] house.
Deep [[dread:dread]] filled the nights, and loud booms would [[frighten:frighten]] the small dogs.
A long [[tension:tension]] grew through those [[turbulent:turbulent]] days, until [[quiet:quiet]] talks brought hope.
The past [[turmoil:turmoil]] coloured every true [[scenario:scenario]] they shared inside the warm hall.
That special [[occasion:occasion]] taught everyone to respect [[limit:limits]] on pride and anger.
The old [[boundary:boundary]] stones kept a firm [[rein:rein]] on the horses that strayed.
Teams no longer [[compete:compete]] in shooting [[contest:contests]], but in joyful [[harvest:harvest]] games.
Old [[foe:foes]] learned to [[contend:contend]] kindly, never letting [[rival:rival]] pride [[spoil:spoil]] the [[spring:spring]] work.
One former [[competitor:competitor]] now calls his old [[enemy:enemy]] a cherished, close friend.
Good [[strategy:strategy]] needs wiser [[tactic:tactics]] than hasty guns and [[bitter:bitter]] cries.
Each [[clever:clever]] [[manoeuvre:manoeuvre]] followed Grandpa's simple [[blueprint:blueprint]] for a safe return home.
Grandpa would [[warn:warn]] the children kindly, and hunger once [[compel:compelled]] mothers to weep.
Kind nurses felt [[oblige:obliged]] by [[duty:duty]] to [[order:order]] bread for hungry mouths.
Their calm [[protest:protest]] helped [[refute:refute]] the lies spread by distant radio stations.
True [[might:might]] lies not in [[cruel:cruel]] [[force:force]] but in [[gentle:gentle]] helping hands.
Warm food will [[reinforce:reinforce]] weak bodies, and nothing [[can:can]] [[impair:impair]] such kindly care.
Soft songs [[can:can]] [[mitigate:mitigate]] the torment and bring [[comfort:comfort]] to lonely widows.
Each small [[event:event]] holds some [[matter:matter]] [[worthy:worthy]] of [[quiet:quiet]] adult thought.
Great change [[can:can]] [[happen:happen]] wherever kind deeds [[occur:occur]] daily around the schools.
No [[savage:savage]] act seems [[reckless:reckless]] now beside Grandpa's [[gentle:gentle]] wrinkled smile.
His [[fierce:fierce]] winter cough sounds [[foul:foul]], yet his heart stays kind.
No [[evil:evil]] thought serves the [[devil:devil]] who feeds on angry quarrels.
Harsh [[punishment:punishment]] should never be [[execute:executed]] on boys who stole bread from hunger.
They did not [[hang:hang]] up their tools but [[sacrifice:sacrificed]] sweet sleep to help neighbours.
Each lost [[casualty:casualty]] asks us to [[bury:bury]] our pride along with the rusty shells.
One silent [[funeral:funeral]] ended near a mossy [[grave:grave]] behind the white poplars.
A [[plain:plain]] [[tomb:tomb]] stands far from the noisy [[hell:hell]] of those smoky old fields.
Old [[maritime:maritime]] maps show the [[naval:naval]] routes once used by worried sailors.
A [[quiet:quiet]] [[fleet:fleet]] sleeps offshore, while a tired [[troop:troop]] rests among the green pines.
No [[rough:rough]] [[landing:landing]] shakes the cove where gulls [[hover:hover]] over blue waves.
Slow walkers [[proceed:proceed]] along the stone steps as peace [[progress:progresses]] in every heart.
No [[military:military]] [[truck:truck]] carries [[nuclear:nuclear]] loads through the blossoming apple orchards.
[[bitter:Bitter]] [[poison:poison]] cannot [[devastate:devastate]] the gardens where children plant young saplings.
Each needless [[risk:risk]] steals the calm joy of [[adventure:adventure]] from curious young travellers.
Sudden [[peril:peril]] may foretell [[catastrophe:catastrophe]] for towns that ignore the early signs.
Old bridges need not [[collapse:collapse]] under the [[torture:torture]] of the long rainy seasons.
[[cruel:Cruel]] words [[humiliate:humiliate]] playmates, and lies [[can:can]] [[damage:damage]] young friendships.
Such [[harmful:harmful]] jokes [[mislead:mislead]] newcomers and [[spoil:spoil]] the [[quiet:quiet]] evening classes.
Loud quarrels [[disturb:disturb]] sleepy minds, and boastful shouts [[interfere:interfere]] with the lessons.
Late bells [[interrupt:interrupt]] the games, but kind children never [[retreat:retreat]] from their [[duty:duty]].
Dry leaves [[shrink:shrink]] in the sun, and tired feet [[withdraw:withdraw]] from the dusty roads.
Frail elders [[withstand:withstand]] the cold winds through firm [[compromise:compromise]] among neighbours.
Tired hands [[surrender:surrender]] their knives, while white doves [[escape:escape]] into the clouds.
Sleepy clerks [[quit:quit]] their quarrels, and leaders [[abandon:abandon]] pride for warm handshakes.
We gladly [[forgo:forgo]] harsh slogans and [[discard:discard]] the faded posters of old days.
Clean yards are [[rid:rid]] of weeds, and children [[defend:defend]] the blossoms with care.
Stone walls [[safeguard:safeguard]] the seeds, and [[gentle:gentle]] love will [[defeat:defeat]] cold mistrust.
[[gentle:Gentle]] hands [[resist:resist]] anger, and letters [[capture:capture]] the smiles of distant cousins.
True [[victory:victory]] brings [[quiet:quiet]] [[triumph:triumph]] to simple homes and sunny schools.
Kind hearts [[conquer:conquer]] fear where a white [[monument:monument]] holds its silent names.
A grey [[tablet:tablet]] stands beside a tall [[statue:statue]] in the shady courtyard.
A [[bronze:bronze]] [[medal:medal]] keeps high [[honour:honour]] for the nurses of wartime winters.
Their [[glorious:glorious]] deeds [[contribute:contribute]] light to the clear autumn classrooms each year.
Old friends [[devote:devote]] their evenings and [[owe:owe]] warm thanks to the nameless helpers.
[[night:Night]] [[patrol:patrols]] have turned into friendly watchers of the sleepy village lanes.
Among the blooming peony bushes, faded [[camouflage:camouflage]] now hides no [[obstacle:obstacle]].
Deep [[burrow:burrows]] [[shelter:shelter]] the rabbits, and no crafty [[spy:spy]] walks at [[midnight:midnight]].
Young [[scout:scouts]] follow the paths where one kind [[general:general]] shares warm bread.

sentZh: 上周日爷爷带我们参观战争纪念馆，讲起他童年时代的暴力与漫长冲突。
他说，一天夜里一场突袭让人看清了豪言壮语背后巨大的痛苦。
他讲述了一场冬季战役，最后在结冰的河边打了最后一仗。
弟弟听到那场无声的挣扎和远处的爆炸，忍不住打了个寒战。
士兵们会炮轰镇子，飞机则在夜间飞来轰炸桥梁。
每一次爆炸都震碎窗户，吓得小孩子们躲到桌子底下哭。
直到现在，炉边的一粒小火星仍在爷爷悲伤的记忆里闪烁。
他记得空旷田野里一辆毁坏的坦克散发出的火药味。
展厅里一门重炮静静立着，旁边躺着一枚小导弹。
爷爷轻轻地把一件旧武器和一把磨旧的手枪放回木箱。
旁边躺着一支生锈的步枪和一颗子弹，是那些岁月留下的伤感纪念。
最后他指着旧靶子，它曾帮炮弹偏转，护住附近的家园。
爷爷的第一个任务是送信，一盏灯暖暖的火焰为他引路。
一天傍晚，红色信号弹升起，点点亮光轻轻洒满夜空。
晚饭后，他就着柔和的微光慢慢擦拭自己的刀刃。
然后他把剑和旧斧放在安静的壁炉旁。
他曾用小锤子修好琴弓，让它在寒夜里奏出音乐。
多年后，一张弯箭和一杆长矛静静躺在教室布满灰尘的图画下。
一顶裂开的头盔和一面凹陷的盾牌并排安放在学校门上方。
好心的老师帮孩子们配备物品，还为疲惫的来访者准备热茶。
大厅能提供热汤，还在门口安排了友好的帮手。
从那以后再没有石头砸中墙壁，也没有战鼓为行军的队伍擂响。
再没听过突然的袭击，也没有愤怒的拳头在门上砸出洞。
曾经砍柴的手，绝不会在怒气中刺伤朋友。
那个艰难的两难处境让爷爷全家多年陷于困苦之中。
每个暗藏的陷阱都源于贪婪首领间残酷的阴谋。
街道一片赤贫，漫长的饥荒慢慢蔓延整个山谷。
寒夜夺走了热饭，瘦弱的孩子们只好挨饿。
壮汉们跑来夺取粮食，沿着小巷追赶可怜的农夫。
每一次新的威胁都会冒犯那些热爱安静乡村生活的乡民。
然而再凶的叫嚷也侵犯不了他们那间满是爱的小屋。
没有外人敢越过栅栏擅自闯入，也没人敢踏进他们的院子。
即使愤怒的人群攻击旧日的安宁，家中的规矩也从未被违反。
每次突然的袭击只教会他们用平静耐心的话语回击恶意。
漫长的围困没能用饥饿围住小镇，一名年轻的哨兵守在门口。
即便在谈判长期停顿的日子里，高墙也围不住他们的希望。

microscope.exZh: 他通过显微镜观察这只虫子。

mistress.m: n. 女主人；情妇；女教师（英）

mode.ex: The mode of transportation is a bike.

monument.m: n. 历史遗迹；纪念碑；不朽作品

muddy.m: adj. 泥泞的；模糊不清的

naval.ex: He works on a naval ship.

neighbourhood.m: n. 街坊；四邻；附近地区

neighbourhood.exZh: 我们认识这个街坊里的所有邻居。
neighbourhood.note: 词伙：low density neighbourhoods, whole neighbourhood

nephew.ex: My brother's son is my nephew.

network.ex: The internet is a big network of computers.

network.note: 词伙：public transport networks, social networking websites, build up a network of contacts

niece.ex: My sister's daughter is my niece.

nurse.ex: The nurse gave the patient medicine.

oblige.ex: The law obliges drivers to wear seat belts.
oblige.exZh: 法律迫使司机系安全带。

obstacle.ex: The big rock was an obstacle on the road.
obstacle.exZh: 那块大石头是路上的障碍。

occasion.ex: She wore a dress for the occasion.

offend.ex: He offended the law by stealing.
offend.note: 同义词：insult（侮辱，蓄意羞辱）；upset（惹难过，使心烦）；anger（激怒，使大怒）；词伙：offend calm folks

operate.m: v. 运转；操作；施行手术

orphan.m: n. 孤儿；失去生母的幼小动物

orphan.exZh: 这个男孩和叔叔住在一起，因为他是个孤儿。

owe.ex: He owes his success to hard work.
owe.exZh: 他把他的成功归功于努力工作。

paper.ex: He wrote his name on the paper.

patent.ex: He got a patent for his new invention.
patent.exZh: 他为自己的新发明获得了专利。

patriot.ex: He is a true patriot who loves his country.

patrol.ex: The police patrol the street at night.

pause.ex: There was a short pause before he answered.
pause.exZh: 他回答之前停顿了一下。

peril.ex: The hikers faced great peril in the storm.
peril.exZh: 徒步者在风暴中面临巨大危险。

phase.m: n. 阶段；时期；v. 分阶段进行

pitfall.m: n. 陷阱；隐患；想不到的困难

pivot.m: v. 以…为中心；n. 中心

plight.ex: The family is in a difficult plight after losing their home.
plight.exZh: 这家人在失去家园后陷入了困境。

poison.m: n. 毒药；毒物；v. 毒害
poison.ex: The snake's poison can kill quickly.

polytechnic.m: n. 工艺专科学院；理工专科学院

praise.ex: His hard work received much praise from the teacher.
praise.exZh: 他的努力工作得到了老师的许多赞美。

precise.ex: He gave a precise answer to the question.
precise.exZh: 他对这个问题给出了准确的答案。

prepare.ex: I prepare my lunch every morning.

prevent.ex: Wearing a helmet can prevent head injuries.

prohibit.ex: The school prohibits students from using phones in class.

proof.ex: The math teacher asked for a proof of the theorem.

prophet.ex: The prophet told the people about the coming storm.

proponent.m: n. 支持者；拥护者；辩护者

propose.ex: He proposes to go to the park after lunch.
propose.note: 同义词：advise（建议，劝人如何做）

protest.m: n. 抗议活动；v. 抗议

prototype.ex: The engineer built a prototype of the new car.
prototype.exZh: 工程师制作了这辆新车的原型。

provide.exZh: 父母为孩子们提供食物。

pump.ex: He pumps water from the well every morning.
pump.exZh: 他每天早上从井里抽水。

punch.ex: He punched the wall in anger.

punishment.exZh: 这个男孩因为打碎了窗户而受到了处罚。

pupil.ex: The pupil writes with a pencil in class.

rebel.ex: The rebel fought against the king's rules.
rebel.exZh: 这位叛逆者反抗国王的法令。

reckless.m: adj. 鲁莽的；不计后果的

reckless.exZh: 他开车鲁莽，结果出了事故。

refine.ex: He refines his writing every day.
refine.exZh: 他每天完善自己的写作。

refute.exZh: 他用清晰的证据驳斥了这一说法。

rifle.m: n. 步枪；来复枪（又称来福枪）；v. 快速搜寻

scout.exZh: 侦察兵悄悄观察敌人的动向。

shed.m: n. 棚屋；v. 使脱落；去除

shift.m: v. 转移；换（挡）；n. 轮班

spark.m: n. 火花；火星；v. 激发

spark.exZh: 火柴产生了一个小火花。

spear.ex: The warrior threw a spear at the enemy.
spear.exZh: 战士向敌人投掷了一支矛。

spy.m: n. 间谍；v. 秘密侦察
